g-be35bafa.desc:
Episode 3 of "As Noted," showcasing the finale of JOURNEY. In many respects, this single piece of music birthed my entire career; thatgamecompany's beautiful and uplifting gameplay gave this piece an almost unfair advantage in emotionally communicating with players. From the moment of its 2012 release it has been popular online and, rather astoundingly, in concert halls. Orchestras the world over have performed this piece! Note that showcased here is the *original* orchestration, not the concert adaptation.

For this episode, we focus not only on the notes themselves, but I've annotated the score to showcase how the piece was integrated into the gameplay. It's a mostly-linear series of interconnected loops with transitional "stingers" smoothing it all out. The OST presentation makes none of that clear so hopefully this is interesting!

As always, leave comments to request specific pieces of mine to be featured in "As Noted."

【Main】
****2 Likes / 0 Dislikes****
****Edited 2026-02-26****

I have made the score for educational, personal, and entertaining purpose

I have completed this transcription now. After years passed since the first day I played Terraria. It is a true legend in game history and offers top quality gameplay and OSTs.

Scott Lloyd Shelly is a very creative and talanted composer who uses symphony orchestra structure to compose electronic-based tracks, which makes this indie game stands out high in the peak.

All tracks are short, but has been purposely written with frequent changes in shifts, counterpoints, and rhythms, in order to extend its looping-fatigue cycle. Melodic motions and harmonies are also delicated and never get bored after more than 100th loops.

Since we mostly focus on standard/traditional instruments, this makes every Terraria track become a great challenge for score composer/arranger. However, the process to recreate these strange, unique and intriguing synth sounds fascinates me deeply.

Terraria’s OSTs are clearly only after WoW, skyrim, and Zelda. To think its from a indie game, makes it even greater😆

Special thanks to Bryan Lake and Milisonics from Vital Discord, for recreation of the saw-alike synth. Even it is only 85% similar (my perspective), it is still a valid recreation. The original synths are pretty hard to reverse-engineer
